candidate_evidence.quote: intraarterial administration of carboplatin (400 mg/m2) combined with Caelyx (30 mg/m2) will be compared with intraarterial administration of carboplatin (400 mg/m2) combined with etoposide phosphate (400 mg/m2)
At the heart of the present study, carboplatin, which will be combined with either one of two agents found to be ideally suited in this setting: Caelyx (liposomal doxorubicin) or etoposide phosphate.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: for Progressing Glioblastoma at First or Second Relapse

role_evidence.quote: So much so, that it is nowadays considered a standard of care for relapsing tumours in our institution.
At our institution, carboplatin is the primary chemotherapeutic agent for IA infusions and yields positive tumour responses in 70% of patients for a median PFS of 5 months.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: These reactive complexes react with DNA bases to create inter- and intrastrand crosslinks which prevent cell division by hindering DNA synthesis.

flag.reason: IA carboplatin is given identically in both experimental arms and described as institutional standard of care, so coded soc_backbone; but it is part of the investigated IA combination and could be viewed as a candidate.

role_evidence.quote: Participants will be treated with IA carboplatin + IA liposomal doxorubicin on each cycle (4-6 weeks), for up to 12 cycles.

agents.drug_class_hint: anthracycline cytotoxic; pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (Caelyx), given intra-arterially
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: DNA binding and cross-linking, interference with DNA strand separation, inhibition of RNA polymerase, inhibition of topoisomerase II, formation of free radicals and membrane peroxidation have all been suggested.

role_evidence.quote: Participants will be treated with IA carboplatin + IA etoposide phosphate on each cycle (4-6 weeks), for up to 12 cycles.

agents.drug_class_hint: topoisomerase II inhibitor cytotoxic; etoposide phosphate (water-soluble prodrug/ester of etoposide), given intra-arterially

coder_notes: Two experimental arms, no control arm; randomised comparison of IA carboplatin + IA pegylated liposomal doxorubicin vs IA carboplatin + IA etoposide phosphate. Registered interventions are combined entries ('IA Carboplatin + IA Caelyx', 'IA Carboplatin + IA Etoposide Phosphate'); agent names split accordingly. Intra-arterial catheter delivery is not treated as device-dependent (no BBB-opening device or activation). Doxorubicin is pegylated liposomal (could also be new_formulation); etoposide phosphate is a prodrug of etoposide (could also be prodrug); new_route chosen for intra-arterial administration. Surgery for cytoreduction before treatment not coded.
